title: Being fired from the Maple Leaf band and replaced by Paul Barbarin
summary: A long story of watching Henry Martin, playing with Bob Lyons, and being fired by the Maple Leaf band for Barbarin and then asked back.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Oh, I see. I was a kid. Oh, I didn't hear that. I know Bunk, when he saw Barney in San Francisco, that was 15 years ago, he said to Barney, you won't remember me, but I remember you. And I used to go to your uncle's house. Okay, yeah. He played violin. He told Barney all about his family more than Barney could remember, he said. That's right. And he said he remembers Barney being a little kid playing around there, but Barney wouldn't remember Bunk. I was a kid too, and I used to admire when my uncle would have rehearsals. And I used to admire being a drummer. And I used to stand by the drummer, there's a Watson drummer, there's a Watson drummer, a Watson drummer. Do you know who they were? I said one day I'd be like that, Henry Martin was playing the drum with the, with Kid Ores and there. Yeah. And I used to admire where Henry Martin played. So I seen when I got to be a big man, and I was out here playing drum, and I'd have it running with the Maple Leaf band, I'd go over where Henry Martin was playing with Bob Lyons band. You might have heard it talk about Bob Lyons. Yes, I knew him up there, Sheshy was there. And I told Bob, I'm out of work, he said, what's the matter? I said, I'd left the Maple Leaf band. He said, well come on and work tonight. That's why he was fired. That's why he was fired. So they used to fire Henry Martin and take me. And if I quit five lines band, I don't care who be playing the Maple Leaf band. I said, oh. I said, my, my, my, my, my work. Tell me, come on and work tonight. That time they fire you right now. You got to work tonight. Come and tell you, don't show up on the job tonight. We got another drummer. That's what he was fired. No two weeks notice or no one day or one week notice, you're fired now. I said I'll laugh sometimes man. I seen I was going to work at the Spencer Maple Leaf Band. We worked for the San Suu Seahawks every Sunday, Wednesdays and Fridays. I was on Howard. And we used to wear tuxedo suits during that time. So I was taking my band, I was knocking on the door, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom. Now we played that Tuesday night on St. Charles Street. So I seen the manager of the band, which was Old Gasper. I said come on in. Came on in. I said what's the trouble? Well he had been drinking a little bit. I said, man you're sick? I said no. I said I've come to tell you. I said what? I said the band decided to take another drummer. I said yeah. I said I think it's right. I said you should have told me last night. I said I could have worked tonight. I could have went to work with Bob Lyons band tonight. I said well, he says the band decided to get the new drummer. I said well who's the new drummer? He said Paul Barbaran. I said yeah. He said well that's alright. So the previous week before that, Mania Corrish was playing trumpet with the American League band at the time. Because Mania just said can't be what she called him. So Mania, he passed the remark. He told Old Gasper, he says there, Oh, he says there's a good drummer coming in time. So I said well who's the good drummer? Well he wouldn't tell me. So I said well, I said what you should do is get the good drummer. So anyway, they fired me and they took Paul Barbaran. So they gave him a gang of dates. We used to carry a little memo pad, memo book. It was full of dates. Well I could have went to work with Bob Lyons. They fired me on a Wednesday night. No, on a Tuesday, because I was supposed to work that Wednesday night. So I come to find out that Friday I was going down home and Old Gasper was living then on Moray between St Anthony and Annette. I said, hey, you're just the one I want to see. I said, yeah. I said, what you want? He said, you want a drink? I said, yeah. I said, yeah. I think I'll drink. So he went to my daddy. I said, come on. I said, let's go in this bar in here. And he bought a pint of whiskey. Well T-Bar was living with his daddy then. T-Bar Barbaran was living on St. Claude between St Anthony and Annette. On that side of the bank, his daddy. He said, no supper. He said, what? He said, the band made me do something I didn't want to do. I said, what's your trouble? He said, the band wants you back. I said, the band wants me back. Want me back for what? I said, y'all got a good drummer? Yeah, but he said, it's not like you. T-Bar Barbaran, we called him T-Bar. Paul, we called him T-Bar. T-Bar Barbaran getting up there and making a whole lot of monkeys shine. He's dropping sticks on the floor. He's running around the beige drum. He's breaking the time. The people, T-Bar used to call me a little Chinese. I was kind of small then. You know, I was kind of thin, you know. We want Chinese back. We want Chinese back. We want Chinese back. So he says, the band wants you to come back, or? I said, yeah. He said, I'm not coming back. Oh, come on up your way. I said, when the band want me to come back? He said, you start Friday. He said, no. He said, the band want me back? Yeah. I said, I'm going to start tonight. The band want me back. I said, I want to do Bob Brand the same thing that Bob Brand done making. So Bob Brand was sitting on his daddy's step. And when I went in the bar with this fellow Oak Gatham, he waved at me a lot. He waved at him a lot. Waved at him too. We come back. We stand and talk. He said, come on with me over there. I said, look. I ain't going with you over there. I said, T-Boy didn't come to my house with you to tell me not to show up on the job tonight. I said, why is that I got to go over there with you to tell him not to show up on the job tonight? He said, all right, wait for him at the corner. I said, okay. He went and told T-Boy Bar Brand and said, well. He says, the band decided to take Nellie back. He said, I know that. He said, I could see that last night. He said, all the whole band got together and they were stalking and they were shooshooing. He said, look. He said, oh man, don't you ever come try to hire me no more. So, and then I went back to the Maple Leaf Band to the Maple Leaf Band and broke up. When was Dave Ogden with him? I don't remember. I don't remember Dave Ogden being with the Maple Leaf Band.
Who did he play with him?
